title: En el médico — at the doctor
summary: A man describes what hurts, for how long, and what he has already taken. The past tense, and the vocabulary you cannot afford to be vague about.

lines.speaker: A
lines.translation: Good afternoon. Sit down. What is the matter?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Me duele mucho el estómago desde hace tres días.
lines.translation: My stomach has hurt a lot for three days.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sí, anoche tuve treinta y ocho y medio.
lines.translation: Yes, last night I had thirty-eight and a half.

lines.speaker: A
lines.translation: Have you vomited? Do you have diarrhoea?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Vomité ayer dos veces. Diarrea no.
lines.translation: I was sick twice yesterday. No diarrhoea.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Tomé una pastilla para el dolor, pero no me hizo nada.
lines.translation: I took a painkiller, but it did nothing for me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.translation: Are you allergic to any medicine?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bien. Beba mucha agua y descanse. Si sigue igual mañana, vuelva.
lines.translation: Good. Drink plenty of water and rest. If it is the same tomorrow, come back.

vocabulary.meaning: … hurts me — the thing that hurts is the subject: me duele la cabeza, me duelen los pies
allergic to — say this before anything else if it is true

questions.q: How long has his stomach hurt?
What temperature did he have last night?
Which of these does he have?
questions.explain: Vomité ayer dos veces. Diarrea no.

questions.q: What does the doctor tell him to do?
options: Drink water, rest, come back if no better
